_meta.indication: Treatment of adult patients with chronic phase, accelerated phase, or blast phase CML that is resistant or intolerant to prior TKI therapy, or Ph+ALL that is resistant or intolerant to prior TKI therapy. The indication is based on response rate.

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: Multi-center, international, single-arm, open-label trial; patients enrolled in 6 cohorts by disease type and T315I mutation status; all received a 45 mg once-daily starting dose.
pivotal_trials.population: Previously treated patients with CML (chronic, accelerated, or blast phase) or Ph+ALL resistant or intolerant to prior TKI therapy, including those with the BCR-ABL T315I mutation.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Major Cytogenetic Response (MCyR) for CP-CML cohorts; Major Hematologic Response (MaHR) for AP-CML, BP-CML, and Ph+ALL cohorts.
pivotal_trials.result: CP-CML MCyR 54% (144/267) overall (49% resistant, 70% T315I); AP-CML MaHR 52% (43/83) overall (55% resistant, 39% T315I); BP-CML MaHR 31% (19/62); Ph+ALL MaHR 41% (13/32).

nct_ctgov.title: Ponatinib for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML) Evaluation and Ph+ Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL)

key_safety: Most common non-hematologic adverse reactions (>=20%): hypertension, rash, abdominal pain, fatigue, headache, dry skin, constipation, arthralgia, nausea, and pyrexia; hematologic reactions include thrombocytopenia, anemia, neutropenia, lymphopenia, leukopenia. Serious arterial thrombosis occurred in 8% (34/449); serious bleeding events in 5% (22/449); severe (grade 3/4) myelosuppression in 48% (215/449).
target_moa: Ponatinib is a kinase inhibitor that inhibits the tyrosine kinase activity of ABL and T315I mutant ABL (IC50 0.4 and 2.0 nM), as well as additional kinases including VEGFR, PDGFR, FGFR, Eph receptor, SRC family members, KIT, and RET.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: ARTERIAL THROMBOSIS and HEPATOTOXICITY. Serious arterial thrombosis (cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, peripheral vascular), including fatal MI and stroke, occurred in 8% of patients; hepatotoxicity, liver failure, and death have occurred.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the product was not taken to an Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee.

citations.quote: This indication is based upon response rate [see *Clinical Studies* (14)]. There are no trials verifying an improvement in disease-related symptoms or increased survival with Iclusig.

- The primary endpoint for patients with CP-CML was Major Cytogenetic Response (MCyR). The MCyR rate was 54% (144/267) overall in patients with CP-CML; 49% (99/203) in the resistant cohort and 70% (45/64) in the T315I cohort.

summary.text: Iclusig received accelerated approval under 21 CFR 314.500 based on response rate from the single-arm Phase 2 PACE trial (Study 10-201), with a priority review and prior fast track designation (granted 30 November 2010 for T315I-mutant CML/Ph+ALL) and orphan drug designation; confirmatory follow-up of the single-arm trial to 24 months was required.

citations.quote: We have completed our review of this application. It is approved under the provisions of accelerated approval regulations (21 CFR 314.500), effective on the date of this letter, for use as recommended in the enclosed agreed-upon labeling text. Marketing of this drug product and related activities must adhere to the substance and procedures of the referenced accelerated approval regulations.

The basis for accelerated approval is a single Phase 2 clinical trial, Study 10-201 (PACE trial), a single-arm, international clinical trial where the efficacy and safety of Iclusig was demonstrated in cohorts of patients with CML (all phases) or Ph+ ALL.
